SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p238/r2.claim: Dropping the n from yakun in the question about a drop of semen is another instance of omission shaped by haste.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.claim: It names two stages of human creation, the semen drop and the clot.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r2.anchor: وذكر طورين من أطوار خلق الإنسان، وهما النطفة والعلقة

NAHHAS:v5p92/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r16.claim: The masculine agreement refers to maniyy, the nearer noun; the feminine form can agree with nutfa.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r16.anchor: على تذكير المني وهو أقرب إليه و تمنى للنطفة

SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r1.claim: The common reading uses yāʾ in يك, referring back to the human being.
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r1.anchor: العامة على الياء من تحت في " يك " رجوعا للإنسان.

SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r2.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads يك with tāʾ of direct address, a rhetorical turn that rebukes the addressee.
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r2.anchor: والحسن بتاء الخطاب على الالتفات إليه توبيخا له

SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r3.speaker: حفص
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r3.claim: In Ḥafṣ’s يمنى reading, the pronoun may refer to semen, meaning ‘is poured’; the clause is then genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r3.anchor: قرأ حفص " يمنى " بالياء من تحت، وفيه وجهان: أحدهما: أن الضمير عائد على المني، أي: يصب، فتكون الجملة في محل جر.

SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows the pronoun to refer to the drop, since its feminine gender is nonliteral and it means water; al-Samīn says this works only on Ibn Kaysān’s view, while grammarians call it poetic necessity, as in the cited line with أبقل.
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنه يعود للنطفة؛ لأن تأنيثها مجازي، ولأنها في معنى الماء، قاله أبو البقاء، وهذا إنما يتمشى على قول ابن كيسان.

SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r5.claim: The other readers use feminine تمنى, referring to the drop; on this reading, and on the preceding analysis where the pronoun refers to the drop, the clause is an accusative adjective of an accusative noun.
SAMIN-DURR:75:37/r5.anchor: فعلى هذه القراءة وعلى الوجه المذكور قبلها تكون الجملة في محل نصب؛ لأنها صفة لمنصوب.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r1.claim: Dropping the nūn from يكن suits the sūra’s recurring haste: the shorter form lets the verb finish quickly.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r1.anchor: فحذف نون (يكن) للفراغ من الفعل بسرعة وهو الملائم لجو العجلة في السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r2.claim: The shortened يكن also hints that semen alone does not make a human: it must meet the ovum, and semen is only part of the cause.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r2.anchor: فنقَصَ من فعل الكون إشارة إلى أن التطوير المذكور في الآيات هذه لا يكون إلا بهما معاً، أما المني فهو جزء من السبب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r3.claim: يمنى means that semen is emitted into the womb; without that emission, formation does not occur.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r3.anchor: ومعنى (يُمنَى) : يراق في الرحم، فإن لم يُمنَ فلا تكوين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.claim: The agent is omitted from left aimless, created, fashioned, and made, matching the preceding passive and the sūra’s urgent tone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p235/r4.anchor: وعدم ذكر فاعل الخلق وما بعده مناسب لحذف فاعل الترك. وكل ذلك مناسب لجو العجلة في السورة

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read تمنى with tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r1.anchor: قال: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي: من مني تمنى [القيامة/ 37]

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim, as well as Ibn ʿĀmir, read يمنى with yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r2.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم: يمنى بالياء، وكذلك المفضل عن عاصم، وقرأ ابن عامر: يمنى بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr’s transmissions vary: several named routes report تمنى, Abū Zayd reports both forms, and ʿAbbās says Abū ʿAmr read tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r3.anchor: وروى علي بن نصر واليزيدي وعبد الوارث والنصر بن شميل عن هارون عن أبي عمرو

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r4.claim: With tāʾ, the verb refers to the feminine نطفة; 53:46, من نطفة إذا تمنى, confirms this feminine subject and supports the tāʾ reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r4.anchor: من قال: من مني تمنى حمله على النطفة: ألم يك نطفة تمنى من مني

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r5.claim: With yāʾ, the verb refers to مني, as though saying semen is poured or decreed; human creation and other outcomes are determined from it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r5.anchor: أي: يقدر خلق الإنسان وغيره منها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r6.claim: He cites an unattributed poem with منت and another with المنا as evidence for the root’s sense of destiny; the second is explicitly glossed as ساقه القدر.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r6.anchor: لعمر أبي عمرو لقد ساقه المنا إلى جدث يوزى له بالأهاضب أي: ساقه القدر

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r7.claim: A further unattributed line, منت لك أن تلقى ابن هند منية, is cited alongside the same root-based explanation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p346#2/r7.anchor: منت لك أن تلقى ابن هند منية وفارس مياس إذا ما تلببا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r6.claim: Readers agree on tāʾ in تمنى, referring to the implied nutfa; Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim alone reads yāʾ, referring to semen.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p357#2/r6.anchor: اجمع القراء فيه على التاء ردا على المعنى الا ما رواه حفص عن عاصم بالياء ردا على النطفة

QIRAAT-ER:75:37:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:75:37:6#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:75:37:6#1/r1.claim: The Imp feminine passive tumnā agrees with feminine nuṭfah rather than masculine maniyy, shifting the syntactic center of emission.
QIRAAT-ER:75:37:6#1/r1.anchor: Canonical feminine passive: agreement can shift from masculine مَنِيّ to feminine نُطْفَةً, changing the syntactic center of emission

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r1.claim: This new sentence rebuts the denial of resurrection by citing the human being’s original creation as evidence against deeming re-creation impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r1.anchor: استئناف وارد لإبطال المذكور فإن مداره لما كان استبعادهم للإعادة دفع ذلك ببدء الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb with second-person tāʾ, a shift of address.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ألم تك بباء الخطاب على سبيل الالتفات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r3.claim: Most readers use feminine tumna, referring to the nutfa that the man ejaculates and deposits in the womb.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأكثر تمنى بالتاء الفوقية فالضمير للنطفة أي يمنيها الرجل ويصبها في الرحم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r4.speaker: حفص وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وسلام والجحدري وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r4.claim: Ḥafṣ, Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, Yaʿqūb, Sallām, al-Jaḥdarī, and Ibn Muḥayṣin read yumnā with yāʾ, referring to the semen.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149#4/r4.anchor: وعلى قراءة الياء هي قراءة حفص وأبي عمرو بخلاف عنه ويعقوب وسلام والجحدري وابن محيصن للمني

BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r12.claim: The next verse’s contraction drops the nūn of yakun to signal urgency and the lowly insignificance of the human’s origin.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p256/r12.anchor: حاذفا نون الكون إعلاما بأن الأمر في هذه النتيجة العظمى ضاق عن أقل شيء يمكن الاستغناء عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.claim: Repeating the question reinforces the rebuke to deniers after the account of Judgment and its reckoning, like 23:115; it prepares for the material proof in 75:37.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p365/r3.anchor: وفي إعادة { أيحسب الإنسان } تهيئة لما سيعقب من دليل إمكان البعث من جانب المادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r4.claim: Verses 37–40 argue that creating a human from weak material through successive stages proves God can recreate him after his parts decay; this prepares the question in 75:40 and echoes 21:104.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r4.anchor: أي أن خلق الإنسان من مادة ضعيفة وتدرجه في أطوار كيانه دليل على إثبات القدرة على إنشائه إنشاء ثانيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.claim: The material argument explains leaving someone without revival; it does not separately elaborate leaving someone without recompense, since revival is for recompense. Sudā had already inserted the wisdom argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p366/r5.anchor: وهذا البيان خاص بأحد معنيي الترك في الآية وهو تركه دون إحياء وأكتفي ببيان هذا عن بيان المعنى الآخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Abu Bakr from Asim read tumnā with tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم تمنى بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r2.claim: Ibn Amir, Hafs from Asim, and Yaqub read yumnā with yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب يمنى بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r3.claim: Abu Amr allows either of the two readings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r3.anchor: وعن أبو عمرو كالقراءتين وقد شرحنا هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#7/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers to his explanation of this reading issue at al-Najm 53:24.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read the verb with yāʾ: the semen is poured into the womb.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r1.anchor: بالياء ابن عامر وحفص أي يراق المنى في الرحم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r2.claim: With tāʾ, the verb refers back to the drop (nutfah).
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#14/r2.anchor: في الرحم وبالتاء يعود إلى النطقة

BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet seized and shook Abū Jahl at al-Baṭḥāʾ, warned him, and Abū Jahl boasted of his invulnerability; at Badr he was felled by the sons of ʿAfrāʾ and finished by Ibn Masʿūd.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r1.anchor: وروى إنه لما نزلت هذه الآية أخذ رسول الله بمجامع ثوب أبي جهل بالبطحاء وهزه مرة أو مرتين

BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.claim: Aqaṣahu means to kill someone in place, while ajhaza means to finish off a wounded person who is near death.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r2.anchor: اقعصه قتله مكانه وأجهز على الجريح أثبت قتل وأسره وتمم عليه

BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.claim: The Prophet called every community a Pharaoh and identified Abū Jahl as this community’s Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r3.anchor: وكان رسول الله عليه السلام يقول إن لكل أمة فرعونا وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل

BURSEVI:v10p199/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r10.claim: The verse answers the supposed difficulty of restoration by pointing to the first creation as proof that resurrection can occur.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r10.anchor: فإن مداره لما كان استبعادهم للإعادة استدل على تحققها ببدء الخلق

BURSEVI:v10p199/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r11.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v10p199/r11.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh regards this as a second proof of resurrection, and the interrogative as rebuke.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r11.anchor: وقال ابن الشيخ هو استدلال على صحة البعث بدليل ثان والاستفهام بمعنى التوبيخ

BURSEVI:v10p199/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r12.claim: Nuṭfa is a little or much amount of clear water; manī is the reproductive fluid of man and woman from which an animal is formed.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r12.anchor: والنطفة بالضم الماء الصافي قل أو كثر والمني ماء الرجل والمرأة أي ما خلق منه حيوان

BURSEVI:v10p199/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r13.claim: With yāʾ, yumnā describes manī; with tāʾ, it describes nuṭfa, and in either case means poured into the womb.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r13.anchor: ويمنى بالياء صفة منى وبالتاء صفة نطفة بمعنى يصب ويراق في الرحم

BURSEVI:v10p199/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r14.claim: Minā is said to take its name from the blood of sacrificial animals poured there.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r14.anchor: لما يمنى فيها من دماء القرابين

BURSEVI:v10p199/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p199/r15.claim: The wording belittles the human’s lowly origin while displaying God’s power to turn it into a well-formed person.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r15.anchor: نبه سبحانه بهذا على خسة قدر الإنسان أولا وكمال أقدرته ثانيا

BURSEVI:v10p199/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p199/r16.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p199/r16.claim: Another view says yumnā emphasizes the human’s contemptible origin and asks how such a creature can rebel against God; the wording hints at an indecent fact, as in the statement that Jesus and Mary ate food.
BURSEVI:v10p199/r16.anchor: وقال بعضهم فائدة قوله يمنى للإشارة إلى حقارة حاله

RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r1.claim: A nutfa is a small amount of water, here a little fluid in the man's loins and the woman's ribs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r1.anchor: المسألة الأولى : النطفة هي الماء القليل وجمعها نطاف ونطف ، يقول : ألم يك ماء قليلا

RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r2.claim: “Poured” means ejaculated into the womb; the verb is also discussed at the cited verses about semen being emitted.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r2.anchor: وقوله : { من منى يمنى } أي يصب في الرحم ، وذكرنا الكلام في يمنى عند قوله

RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r3.claim: Mentioning that the semen is poured subtly recalls its lowly origin and the filthy outlet it passes through; a creature made from it should not rebel against God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r3.anchor: قلنا : فيه إشارة إلى حقارة حاله ، كأنه قيل : إنه مخلوق من المني

RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r4.claim: The lowly bodily function is expressed indirectly, as when the Qur'an says Jesus and Mary ate food, alluding to their need to relieve themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r4.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى في عيسى ومريم : { كانا يأكلان الطعام } ( المائدة : 75 )

RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r5.claim: The verb has a tāʾ reading with the feminine nutfa as subject (“is poured”), or a yāʾ reading with semen as subject, meaning man's creation is decreed from it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p207/r5.anchor: المسألة الثانية : في يمنى في هذه السورة قراءتان التاء والياء ، فالتاء للنطفة

TABRISI:75:26-28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:26-28/r1.speaker: حفص ورويس والباقون
TABRISI:75:26-28/r1.claim: Hafs and Ruways read yumnā with yāʾ, referring to semen; the other readers use tāʾ, referring to the feminine nutfa, as Abu Ali explains, with poetry illustrating the usage.
TABRISI:75:26-28/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص ورويس يمنى بالياء والباقون بالتاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r9.claim: The human is the person just mentioned; nutfa is a small amount of water, and yumnā means poured into the womb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r9.anchor: {ألم يك}، أي: هذا الإنسان. {نطفة}، أي: ماء قليلا، يعني في ابتداء خلقه. {من مني يمنى} أي تصب في الرحم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r10.claim: The author refers back to his explanations of yumnā in the verses about what is emitted from semen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r10.anchor: وذكر الكلام في {من مني يمنى} عند قوله: {من نطفة إذا تمنى (46)} [النجم: 46]، وقوله (¬6): {أفرأيتم ما تمنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p526#2/r11.claim: Yumnā has tāʾ and yāʾ readings: tāʾ agrees with nutfa, while yāʾ agrees with maniyy and describes the source from which the human is formed.

BURHAN:v1p147#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p147#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p147#2/r1.claim: In the Qur'anic inventory of the form yak without a nūn after kāf, the Qiyāma occurrence is cited as al-m yak nuṭfatan; other occurrences are listed across several sūras.

TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.claim: The denier of resurrection began as a small amount of semen in a man; this origin demonstrates God’s power to recreate after death.
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r1.anchor: ألم يك هذا المنكر قدرة الله على إحيائه من بعد مماته

TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r2.claim: Most Medinan and Kufan readers read تمنى with feminine agreement, referring to the drop; some Meccan and Basran readers read يمنى, referring to semen. Both readings are sound in meaning.
TAB-FULL:v23p526#2/r2.anchor: فقرأه عامة قراء المدينة والكوفة: (تمنى) بالتاء

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r3.claim: The subject of kāna is an implicit pronoun referring back to the human being.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r3.anchor: اسم كان ضمير راجع إلى الإنسان

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r4.claim: Imnāʾ of semen means pouring it into the womb.

TABRISI:75:37-40/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:37-40/r2.claim: His own changing states show a wise creator completed his reason and capacity and gave him desire; God would not leave him without religious responsibility.
TABRISI:75:37-40/r2.anchor: كيف يظن أن يهمل وهو يرى في نفسه ومن تنقل الأحوال ما يمكنه أن يستدل به على أن له صانعا حكيما

TABRISI:75:37-40/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:37-40/r3.claim: Yumnā can mean decreed or apportioned.

TABRISI:75:37-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:37-40/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:37-40/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means poured into the womb.

THALABI:v10p92/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p92/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن محيصن وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وسلام
THALABI:v10p92/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Muhaysin, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, and Salam read yumnā with yāʾ; the reading is also transmitted from al-Mufaddal and Hafs from ʿAsim.
THALABI:v10p92/r2.anchor: قرأ الحسن وابن محيص وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وسلام بالياء وهي رواية المفضل وحفص عن عاصم

THALABI:v10p92/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p92/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v10p92/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayd prefers the yāʾ reading because it agrees with the masculine noun manī.

THALABI:v10p92/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p92/r4.speaker: الباقون وأبو حاتم
THALABI:v10p92/r4.claim: The remaining readers use tāʾ because it agrees with the feminine noun nuṭfa, which Abu Hatim prefers.
THALABI:v10p92/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء لأجل النطفة وهو اختيار أبي حاتم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r7.claim: The person began as semen poured into the womb.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:30-40/r7.anchor: { ألم يك نطفة من مني يمنى } يصب في الرحم.

ELMALILI:75:36-40/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r2.claim: Reminding the human of his origin as a drop disproves the assumption that he will be left without purpose and prepares the concluding resurrection proof.
ELMALILI:75:36-40/r2.anchor: Mezkur zannın butlânını isbat ile hâtimeye ihzardır.

FARRA:v3p211/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r13.claim: Both يُمنى with ya and تُمنى with ta are valid: the first agrees with مني, the second with نطفة; Abdullah's companions and some Medinans read ta.
FARRA:v3p211/r13.anchor: من قال: يمنى، فهو للمنى، وتمنى للنطفة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r6.claim: Zajjāj moves from rejecting an aimless life to demonstrating Resurrection through God's power to initiate creation.

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r7.claim: The verb is read tumna, agreeing with feminine nuṭfa, or yumnā, agreeing with masculine maniyy.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r11.speaker: الزركشي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r11.claim: Al-Zarkashi says dropping nūn can point to a thing’s small, humble beginning: the human starts as a drop, then develops into a manifest disputant.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5/r11.anchor: وجاء في (البرهان) للزركشي أن حذف النون في نحو هذا قد يكون "تنبيهاً على صغر مبدأ الشيء وحقارته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p649/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p649/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p649/r2.claim: The nūn is omitted in يك because the sperm is still incomplete and unfertilized, matching the incomplete state and unfinished event.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p649/r2.anchor: حذفت النون هنا لأن النطفة هي من الذكر وهي غير مكتملة بعد وغير مخصّبة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.claim: The Quran also reasons from human development from semen through a clinging clot and formation, including the creation of male and female, to God's power to resurrect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1069/r4.anchor: أحياناً يستدل بالحياة الآخرة على خلق الإنسان وتطوره (أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنَى (37) ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى (38)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.claim: God can re-create the dead, having first made man from a sperm drop, perfected him, and granted him various abilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p63/r6.anchor: it was the Almighty Who created him from a drop of sperm and perfected him and blessed him with various abilities.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r3.claim: The semen is poured into the womb.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم، والحسن، والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r4.claim: Hafs from Asim and al-Hasan read يمنى with yāʾ; the other readers use tāʾ to agree with the feminine noun نطفة.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p287/r4.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم "يمنى" بالياء، وهي قراءة الحسن، وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء، لأجل النطفة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r1.claim: A person began as a drop of semen that was emitted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:37-39/r1.anchor: ألم يك نطفة من منى يمنى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r1.claim: The tiny initial drop is semen from the man's loins and the woman's breastbones, deliberately apportioned by God and emitted through desire as a trial of human origins.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r1.anchor: أي ماء من صلب الرجل وترائب المرأة مقصود ومقدر من الله لابتلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r2.claim: The passive construction reflects that semen is emitted into the womb without the person's choice, as if he had no agency in it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r2.anchor: حتى أن وقت صبها في الرحم انصبت منه بغير اختياره حتى كأنه لا فعل له فيها أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r11.claim: The sūra's conclusion returns to its opening by joining the collection of bones with resurrection for the Day of Gathering.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p257/r11.anchor: وقد رجع آخر السورة على أولها أتم رجوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r1.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r1.claim: The majority read ألم يك with a lower-case ya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r1.anchor: «ألم يك» بالياء من تحت، وقرأ الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r2.claim: Hasan reads ألم تك with feminine ta.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: «ألم تك» بالتاء من فوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r3.claim: A nutfa is a drop of water, whether the amount is little or much; مني is semen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r3.anchor: القطعة من الماء. يقال ذلك للقليل والكثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r4.speaker: ابن عامر، حفص، أبو عمرو، ابن محيصن، الجحدري، سلام، يعقوب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r4.claim: These authorities read يمنى with ya, referring to semen; it may be passive of a man ejaculating or derive from God creating and determining creatures.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم وأبو عمرو بخلاف وابن محيصن والجحدري وسلام ويعقوب: «يمنى» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r5.speaker: جمهور السبعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r5.claim: Most of the Seven and other readers use تمنى with ta, referring to the nutfa; this form likewise admits both explanations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p407/r5.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة والناس. «تمنى» بالتاء، يراد بذلك النطفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r4.claim: The human began as a weak, insignificant drop of fluid, emitted from the loins into the womb; this humble origin supports the argument for resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283#2/r4.anchor: أي: أما كان الإنسان نطفة ضعيفة من ماء مهين، يمنى يراق من الأصلاب في الأرحام.

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r5.claim: Nuṭfah is the male reproductive fluid from which a person is created; the word originally means a small amount of water, though it can also refer to more.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r5.anchor: والمني: هو النطفة، الماء الذي يخلق منه الإنسان

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r13.claim: A person who sees his changing stages of creation should know he has a wise maker; after granting maturity, reason, ability, and desire, God would not leave him without religious duties.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r13.anchor: وهو يرى في نفسه من تنقل الأحوال ما يدل أن له صانعا حكيما

JISHUMI:v10p7196/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r14.claim: Yumnā may mean measured or determined, or emitted from the male sexual organ.
JISHUMI:v10p7196/r14.anchor: يمنى قيل: يقدر، وقيل: يخرج من ذكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r7.claim: One explanation of yumna is that semen is poured out; Mina is said to take its name from the spilling of blood there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r7.anchor: أن معنى يمنى يراق , ولذلك سميت منى لإراقة الدماء فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r8.speaker: يزيد بن عامر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r8.claim: A second explanation is that yumna means to be brought forth or created; Yazid’s verse uses it for what the maker brings about.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r8.anchor: ومنه قول يزيد بن عامر : فاسلك طريقك تمشي غير مختشع حتى تلاقي ما يمني لك الماني

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r9.claim: A third explanation is that it means to combine, referring to the mingling of male and female fluid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r9.anchor: بمعنى يشترك أي اشتراك ماء الرجل بماء المرأة

MUQATIL:75:34-40/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r4.claim: The human being begins as a drop of emitted semen.
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r4.anchor: { ألم يك } هذا الإنسان { نطفة من مني يمنى } [آية: 37] { ثم كان } بعد النطفة { علقة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r4.claim: The nutfa is a drop of semen poured into the womb; manā is linked to spilling blood, and nutfa denotes a little water.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r4.anchor: أي من قطرة ماء تمنى في الرحم، أي تراق فيه ولذلك سميت منى لإراقة الدماء

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r5.claim: Nutfa is a small amount of water; natafa means drip, and the drop comes from the man’s loins and woman’s ribs.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r5.anchor: والنطفة: الماء القليل يقال: نطف الماء: إذا قطر

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r6.speaker: حفص
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r6.claim: Hafs, Ibn Muhaysin, Mujahid, Yaʿqub and ʿAyyash from Abu ʿAmr read with yāʾ to match manī; Abu ʿUbayd selects it.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r6.anchor: وقرأ حفص «من مني يمنى» بالياء، وهي قراءة ابن محيصن ومجاهد ويعقوب وعياش عن أبي عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r7.claim: Other readers use tāʾ to match nutfa, which Abu Hatim selects.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r7.anchor: الباقون بالتاء لأجل النطفة. واختاره أبو حاتم
